core.why: Every project needs coordination, context hygiene, and a handoff contract, from games to SaaS.

opcionais.docs-librarian: when docs/ grows beyond roughly 20 files and answering small questions requires broad reading

web-saas.why: Web app with a backend: TanStack/Next + Supabase/Postgres, public pages and an authenticated area.

mobile-expo.why: React Native app with Expo, usually with a Supabase backend and its own domain logic.

godot-game.why: Godot game: scenes/node tree, GDScript, and headless verification.

unreal-game.why: Unreal game: Actor/Component, Blueprint versus C++, and an asset-heavy pipeline.

scrum-master.purpose: Team lead and sole agent communicating with the user: reads the backlog, writes tasks with risk classes, delegates, verifies handoffs, commits DONE work, evolves the team, and reports.
scrum-master.why: Team lead and sole agent communicating with the user: reads the backlog, writes tasks with risk classes, delegates, verifies handoffs, commits DONE work, evolves the team, and reports.

docs-janitor.purpose: Moves, archives, splits, and indexes non-canon documents byte for byte so agents do not load history just to find current state.
docs-janitor.why: Only performs context hygiene in non-canon docs: writes tasks/archive/agent-ops, never canon, ADRs, architecture, research, briefs, code, or .claude. A project may explicitly expand its prefix to all of docs/.

docs-librarian.purpose: Answers what documents say about a topic in at most 300 words, with file/section, short quotation, and status label; read-only, avoiding full-canon loading by other agents.
docs-librarian.why: Produces text returned to the caller, never a file. Writing would create a second source of authority over canon the role should only cite.

task-author.purpose: Turns a roadmap milestone into the complete TASK-NNN tree with one owner, dependencies, risk, and falsifiable criteria before execution; writes only in docs/tasks/.
task-author.why: Writes specifications, never code. docs/tasks/ covers its outputs; canon, .claude/, and TASK-TEMPLATE are denied because the role reads but does not own them. No Bash means no shell tier.

spec-auditor.purpose: Read-only auditor comparing delivery against canon, earlier deliveries, and documented versus actual behavior; requires two cited pieces of evidence per finding.
spec-auditor.why: Reviewers do not write. Findings belong in the return/handoff; write access would let reviewers fix the discrepancy they should report and bypass human adjudication.

context-scout.purpose: Reports what canonical documents say, with classifications and sources, and locates code symbols within a hard budget of six tool calls and 300 words.
context-scout.why: A context reader whose body forbids opinions and whose frontmatter denies Write/Edit/Bash/NotebookEdit/Agent/WebSearch/WebFetch. Write scope would exceed its role and turn a low-cost answer into canon.

code-reviewer.purpose: Read-only reviewer covering STRUCTURE (architectural coherence) and REGRESSION (silent costs of changes) on the same diff, replacing a separate regression auditor.
code-reviewer.why: A writable reviewer can fix its own finding and lose independence. Empty write scope; shell limited to git status/diff/log/show/blame. Everything else returns through the handoff.

platform-dev.why: Scope follows responsibility boundaries, not convenience.
